propositions: warn_if_cache_ineffective fires on prompts below the 4096-token cache floor where caching cannot work, causing false-alarm warnings despite zero counters being correct and expected behavior
the function's predicate checks only input_tokens > 0 without a lower bound, unable to distinguish a genuinely non-cacheable sub-floor prompt from a cacheable prompt that silently failed to cache
per-call warnings fire ~20 times per rebar review-plan run on sub-floor calls while aggregate run telemetry shows cache_write_tokens > 0, contradicting the claim that caching had no effect
the codebase already knows the cache floor exists (CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096 in pass1.py) but the warning path never consulted it, creating a design inconsistency
gating the warning on input_tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS and single-sourcing the constant eliminates false positives while preserving detection of genuinely cacheable prompts that fail to cache
